expectations.text: Audience characterized at a useful specificity — narrow enough that some direction shapes are clearly right and some clearly wrong
expectations.evidence: Section 1 characterizes the ICU nurse with role, shift structure, CCRN credentialing, cognitive state, and professional values; sufficient specificity to filter directions.

expectations.text: Current state of the landscape named — what tools or services the audience uses today, and the named ways those tools fail
expectations.evidence: Section 3 names paper brain sheets, EHR handoff modules (Epic, Cerner), vendor apps (CareAligned, Voalte), and verbal handoff each with their specific failure modes.

expectations.text: Real research signals only — aggregate signals, sourced findings, paraphrased user behavior; no fabricated quotes; no composite case studies with first-name attribution
expectations.evidence: Includes fabricated specific quotes like 'Bed 12, Mrs. K, day 4 post-op CABG, came in for chest pain, now on low-dose Levo, mentating well' and 'She's been a little tachy when her son leaves, watch for that' presented as illustrative dialog without sourcing; references 'from observation across the literature and informal report' without citation.

expectations.text: Citations or (Inferred) markers on empirical claims — sources cited where claims are empirical; (Inferred) marks extensions
expectations.evidence: Many empirical claims lack citations (the '~30% reduction in medical errors' is only attributed to 'I-PASS RCT' loosely; '34%' workaround rate is absent; many empirical claims like '~7 minutes per patient' have no source). No (Inferred) markers.

expectations.text: Source-quality hierarchy respected AND the highest-tier source available was reached for — primary government, peer-reviewed, or established non-profit sources used where they exist for this domain
expectations.evidence: Loose references to TJC/AHRQ without specific citations; relies heavily on 'observation across the literature and informal report'; no specific peer-reviewed studies named with citation; doesn't reach for the highest-tier sources available.

expectations.text: Strategic, not execution — every claim passes the operational test; no rendering-layer guidance appears
expectations.evidence: Section 5 is heavy execution: 'Two-handed UI patterns (pinch, drag) are hostile. Capacitive touch through nitrile gloves works for most modern phones but is less precise. Targets must be generous'; 'phone screen is small (~6.1")'. These are rendering-layer guidance.

expectations.text: No success criteria smuggled in — quantified targets and KPIs are absent
expectations.evidence: Section 8 summary: 'Earn its 30 seconds per patient and not ask for 31' — this is a quantified success target for the design. Also: 'A handoff tool that adds 90 seconds per patient is dead on arrival; one that saves 30 seconds per patient and never loses signal will be defended fiercely.'

expectations.text: No direction candidates smuggled in for the design — solution-shape proposals for the design are absent; landscape players (what the audience confronts today) is fine
expectations.evidence: Section 6 'Adjacent precedent worth looking at (and what to take from it)' explicitly lists CRM, kneeboards, chyron, OR surgical timeout as design models — direction candidates for the design. Section 7 'Open empirical questions': 'Does the tool live on the phone, the WOW, or both?' surfaces direction-shape choices for the design.

expectations.text: No execution-layer guidance — no typography, contrast, sizing, motion, ARIA, copy-pattern specifics
expectations.evidence: Section 5.1: 'Targets must be generous', specific screen sizing (~6.1"), 'A screen that flashes high mortality risk at the foot of the bed is unacceptable' — copy/rendering specifics; 'Two-handed UI patterns (pinch, drag) are hostile' — interaction-pattern specifics.

Document is structured as 8 major numbered sections with many subsections and bullet lists (sections 1.1-1.4, 2.1-2.4, 3.1-3.5, 4, 5.1-5.4, 6, 7, 8) totaling ~220 lines. Far exceeds the 4-6 short paragraph target.
